(1) the optimal data partitioning strategy for the BWA-GatK pipeline is to partition the reads by their alignment position; (2) the optimal data parallelism for BWA is to partition by the number of threads; (3) the optimal data-parallelism for GATK is to partition by number of samples; (4) the BWA-Gatk pipeline can be run 3 times faster on the same number of compute nodes by using optimal data partitioning and parallel

we have developed a workflow-based model to parallelize the data-intensive tasks of genome alignment and variation calling and we report significant performance improvements by optimizing data partitioning for each task.

(1) the workflow-based approach is a viable solution for parallelization of data intensive tasks; (2) granularity-based data partitioning is an optimal choice for BWA; and (3) alignment-based data partitioning works best for GATK's Halo type Caller.
